mainTopic: Unclear release phrases for wives and slaves, קידושין with a loan or its benefit, and gifts given on condition they be returned
overview: The amud opens by finishing a list of phrases that do nothing, such as telling a שפחה "you are permitted to any man." רבינא proves from a ברייתא about a גט שחרור, using a קל וחומר, that a husband who tells his wife "הרי את לעצמך" has fully divorced her. Next רבינא asks whether "אין לי עסק בך" frees a slave. A ברייתא about an אונו, explained by רב ששת, shows that it does. Then אביי rules that קידושין with a loan does not work. קידושין with the benefit of a loan does work, but it is forbidden as a trick around רבית. The גמרא defines that benefit as giving her more time to repay. רבא's rule about money given on condition it be returned is challenged, and רב אשי restates it: such a gift works everywhere except קידושין, and רבא was quoted that way. The amud ends as רבא begins a new case about a woman who says "give a מנה to so-and-so," which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Phrases that accomplish nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the previous case and adds that telling a שפחה "you are permitted to any man" does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: …he has said nothing. If he said to his maidservant, "You are hereby permitted to any man," he has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list of phrases that have no legal effect. Here it adds a master who tells his שפחה "you are permitted to any man" and rules it means nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each type of release needs its own proper wording. "Permitted to any man" is divorce language, so it does nothing for a slave. Likewise, slave-freeing language does nothing for a wife. The wrong formula for the wrong relationship is just empty words.

keyTerms.meaning: He has said nothing; the words have no legal effect
A female (Canaanite) slave
Permitted to any man; the standard wording of a divorce

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think "permitted to any man" is a weak phrase. It is the core wording of a divorce! It fails here only because it is the wrong kind of formula for freeing a slave.

phrases.english: he has said nothing.
If he said to his maidservant:
"You are hereby permitted to any man"
he has said nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a list of invalid phrases that began before this point on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Divorce wording ("permitted to any man") said to a שפחה has no effect as a release.

steps.title: A husband says: you are for yourself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a husband who tells his wife "הרי את לעצמך" means only her work or a full divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said to his wife, "You are hereby for yourself," what is the law? Do we say he meant only regarding work, or perhaps he meant entirely?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from clear cases to an unclear one. A husband tells his wife "you are for yourself," and the גמרא asks what he meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase has two possible meanings. It could mean "keep your own earnings," which only touches her work. Or it could mean "you are fully on your own," which would be a divorce. The question is which meaning we assume.

keyTerms.meaning: You are hereby for yourself
What is the law?
Regarding work or earnings only
Entirely; a full release
Or perhaps

phrases.english: If he said to his wife:
"You are hereby for yourself," what is the law?
Do we say he said it to her regarding work,
phrases.notes: He means she can keep what she earns, while they stay married.

phrases.english: or perhaps he said it to her entirely?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהּ לְאִשְׁתּוֹ הֲרֵי אַתְּ לְעַצְמְךָ מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing phrases that clearly fail, the גמרא raises a phrase whose meaning is uncertain.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does "הרי את לעצמך" said to a wife mean a release from work only, or a full divorce?

steps.title: Proof from freeing a slave: all the more so a wife
steps.stepSummary: רבינא cites a ברייתא that "הרי אתה לעצמך" frees a slave, and argues with a קל וחומר that it surely divorces a wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Come hear, as a ברייתא teaches: The essence of a bill of freedom is "You are hereby a free man" or "You are hereby for yourself." Now, a Canaanite slave's body belongs to his master, and still, when the master says "You are for yourself," it means entirely. A wife's body is not owned by her husband, so isn't that all the more true for her?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question with a source. A ברייתא says "you are for yourself" is valid wording for a גט שחרור. He reasons that it must then work for a wife too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The master owns the slave's body, a strong hold that is hard to break. Yet "you are for yourself" still breaks it completely. A husband does not own his wife's body, so his hold is weaker. The same words should certainly release her fully. That is the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; introduces a proof
A document freeing a slave
A free man
A Canaanite slave, owned by his master
His body is owned by the master
Isn't it all the more so? (a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: "הרי את לעצמך" counts as a full release. A slave, whose body is owned, is freed by it, so a wife, whose body is not owned, is surely divorced by it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the strength of the bond being broken matters. If words can break the stronger bond of ownership, they can surely break the weaker one.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear, as it is taught:
The essence of a bill of freedom is:
"You are hereby a free man,"
"You are hereby for yourself."
Now, if a Canaanite slave,
whose body the master owns,
when he says to him "You are hereby for yourself"
he means it entirely,
then a wife, whose body he does not own,
isn't it all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא: גּוּפוֹ שֶׁל גֵּט שִׁחְרוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 using a ברייתא about slaves plus a קל וחומר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "הרי את לעצמך" is a full release, so the wife is divorced.
steps.raayaObject: That "הרי את לעצמך" to a wife means a full divorce.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing "הרי אתה לעצמך" as valid wording of a גט שחרור, combined with a קל וחומר from slave to wife.

steps.title: A master says: I have no business with you
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי whether telling a slave "אין לי עסק בך" frees him fully or only releases him from work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: If one said to his slave, "I have no business with you," what is the law? Do we say "I have no business with you" means entirely, or perhaps he meant regarding work?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks a new question about a different unclear phrase. A master tells his slave "I have no business with you." The גמרא is setting up a discussion of what this phrase means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like before, the phrase can be read two ways. It might mean "you are completely free." Or it might only mean "I won't make you work," while the slave still belongs to the master. Steps 5–7 bring a proof that answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: I have no business with you
What is the law?
His slave

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְעַבְדּוֹ ״אֵין לִי עֵסֶק בְּךָ״ מַאי?
phrases.english: If one said to his slave "I have no business with you," what is the law?
Do we say that "I have no business with you"
he said to him entirely,
or perhaps he said it to him regarding work?
phrases.notes: He'd be letting the slave off from work, but the slave would still be his.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְעַבְדּוֹ אֵין לִי עֵסֶק בְּךָ מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same "entirely or only work" pattern as step 2, now with a different phrase and a slave.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does "אין לי עסק בך" said to a slave free him fully, or only release him from labor?

steps.title: A ברייתא about selling a slave to a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן (or רב חנין from מחוזא) brings a ברייתא to answer רבינא's question. A slave sold to a נכרי goes free and needs a גט שחרור. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, if the owner wrote an אונו, that document itself is the release.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רב אשי (some say it was רב חנין from מחוזא): Come and hear. If someone sells his slave to a non-Jew, the slave goes free, and he needs a document of release from his first master. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: When is this so? When the master did not write him an אונו. But if he wrote him an אונו, that document is his release.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone brings a ברייתא to help answer רבינא's question about "אין לי עסק בך". The proof is not complete yet; the next steps will explain what the key document says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a slave sold to a נכרי needs a real גט שחרור from his first owner. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that a document called אונו counts as that release. If the wording of the אונו turns out to be "אין לי עסק בך", then those words give full freedom.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as proof
A document that frees a slave
A document the first owner wrote for the slave at the time of the sale
When is this said? A phrase that narrows down the earlier rule

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Rav Ashi

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב חָנִין מָחוֹזָאָה לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Chanin from Mechoza said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear:
One who sells his slave to a non-Jew
the slave goes out to freedom,
and he needs a document of release from his first master.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
In what case are these words said?
where he did not write an ono document for him,
but if he wrote an ono document for him,
that itself is his release.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer רבינא's question from step 4
steps.raayaObject: That "אין לי עסק בך" fully frees a slave
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement about the אונו

steps.title: What does the אונו document say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly is written in the אונו.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of an אונו?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the אונו actually says. This sets up the answer that finishes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on the exact wording of the אונו. Only if it contains "אין לי עסק בך" does it answer רבינא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances of the ono document?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the wording of the document mentioned in the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact text written in the אונו

steps.title: רב ששת: the document says "I have no business with you"
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the אונו says: when you run away from him, I have no business with you. This proves those words give full freedom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: He writes to him, "When you run away from him (the non-Jew), I have no business with you."
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת tells us the wording of the אונו, and it is exactly "אין לי עסק בך". This completes the answer to רבינא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said the אונו counts as a full release. Its words are "אין לי עסק בך", so these words must give full freedom, not just freedom from work.

keyTerms.meaning: When you run away from him (from the non-Jewish buyer)

steps.whatToRemember: "אין לי עסק בך" written to a slave is a real release. It gives full freedom, not just freedom from work.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
That he writes to him:
When you run away from him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the non-Jew who bought the slave.

phrases.english: "I have no business with you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 and completes the proof from step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אונו says "אין לי עסק בך", so this wording frees the slave fully
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: "אין לי עסק בך" is a full release for a slave

steps.title: אביי: קידושין with a loan versus with the benefit of a loan
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that קידושין with a loan does not work. קידושין with the benefit of a loan does work, but doing it is forbidden because it is a sneaky way around רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If someone makes קידושין with a loan, she is not מקודשת. With the benefit of a loan, she is מקודשת, but it is forbidden to do this because it is a trick to get around the ban on רבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with אביי's rule about using a loan for קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan is money she already owes. Canceling it gives her nothing new, so it cannot make קידושין. The "benefit" of a loan is something of real value she receives, so it works. But because the lender gains from his loan, it looks like רבית, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes קידושין using money she already owes him
The benefit connected to a loan
A trick to get around the ban on taking interest
Interest on a loan, which the תורה forbids

steps.confusionAlert: "Loan" and "benefit of a loan" sound almost the same, but they are different. The loan itself does not work for קידושין. The benefit of the loan does work, even though it is forbidden.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
One who betroths a woman with a loan
she is not betrothed.
With the benefit of a loan, she is betrothed,
but it is forbidden to do so
because it is a trick to get around interest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the slave discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין with a loan does not work. קידושין with the benefit of a loan works, but it is forbidden as a trick around רבית.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya tries to define "הנאת מלוה" so that it works for קידושין but is still only a trick, not real רבית.

steps.title: What is the benefit of a loan?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case אביי means by "the benefit of a loan".
steps.simpleTranslation: This "benefit of a loan" — what is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what "benefit of a loan" means in אביי's rule. This sets up an attempt to define it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any definition must meet two conditions. It must give her something new, so the קידושין works. And it must be only a trick around רבית, not real interest.

phrases.english: This benefit of a loan, what are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the case behind אביי's term

steps.title: First suggestion: lending four for five, which is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the case is a loan of four coins to be paid back with five, where he cancels the extra coin as קידושין. It rejects this for two reasons: that is real רבית, and canceling it is just like canceling a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he set it up as a loan of four to be repaid with five, that is full-fledged רבית! And also, that is the same as a loan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one explanation of "benefit of a loan" and knocks it down right away with two problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, charging five for four is real רבית, but אביי called it only a trick. Second, canceling the extra coin just erases something she owes him. That is exactly the case of a loan, which אביי said does not make קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: introduces a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject
He set it up as a debt (with interest added)
Full, real interest, not just a trick
That is the same as

phrases.english: If you say that he set it up as a debt,
that he said to her: four for five,
phrases.notes: He lends her four coins, she pays back five, and he cancels the extra coin as קידושין.

phrases.english: that is full-fledged interest.
And furthermore, that is the same as a loan!
phrases.notes: She already owes the extra coin, so canceling it gives her nothing new, just like the plain loan case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּאַזְקְפַהּ, דַּאֲמַר לַהּ אַרְבַּע בְּחַמְשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to step 9 and rejects it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects defining "הנאת מלוה" as forgiving interest that was set up on the loan
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That case is real רבית, not a trick, and forgiving an existing debt is the same as a loan, which does not make קידושין

steps.title: The case is when he gives her more time on the loan
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting the four-for-five case, the גמרא says אביי's case is when the lender extends the due date of her loan and uses that extra time as קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case that is needed is where he gave her extra time to pay back the loan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real answer to the question from step 9. אביי's "benefit of a loan" means the lender gives the woman extra time to repay, and that extra time is the קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Extra time on a loan is a real benefit given to her right now, so the קידושין works. But paying a lender for extra time is a form of רבית, so doing it this way is forbidden. This fits both halves of אביי's rule from step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (for the case we suggested); rather, it is needed for this case
He extended, gave more room
Time; here, the due date of the loan

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's "benefit of a loan" means extending the time of the loan. The קידושין works, but it is forbidden because it looks like paying for extra time, which is רבית.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he extended the time for her.
phrases.notes: When her loan came due, he gave her more time to pay. That extra time is what he gives as קידושין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 10 rejected the four-for-five case, this gives the correct case for אביי's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case is אביי's "benefit of a loan"?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lender extends the repayment time and uses the benefit of that extension as קידושין.

steps.title: Money given on condition it is returned does not work for sale, marriage, or redeeming a son
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that giving money "on condition that you return it" does not count for buying, for קידושין, or for פדיון הבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: "Here is a hundred, on condition that you give it back to me." For a sale, he did not buy. For a woman, she is not married. For redeeming a firstborn son, his son is not redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a new rule. If someone hands over money but makes a condition that it be given back, it does not work in these three cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a sale, in קידושין, and in פדיון הבן, real value has to move from one person to the other. If the money must come back, nothing was really given, so the deal does not take effect. The next step shows one case where רבא rules differently.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of one hundred (דינרים)
On condition that
A sale
Married (through קידושין)
Redeeming a firstborn son from a כהן

phrases.english: Rava said:
"Here is a hundred for you
on condition that you return it to me"
in a sale, he did not acquire;
with a woman, she is not betrothed;
in redemption of a son, his son is not redeemed;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: ״הֵילָךְ מָנֶה עַל מְנָת שֶׁתַּחֲזִירֵהוּ לִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement by רבא, related to the theme of what counts as real giving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money given on condition it be returned does not work for a sale, for קידושין, or for פדיון הבן.

steps.title: With תרומה it does count, but it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues: for תרומה, giving on condition it is returned does count as giving, but it is forbidden because the כהן looks like one who helps at the threshing floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: With תרומה, he has done the מצוה of giving. But it is forbidden to do this, because it looks like a כהן who helps out at the threshing floors.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his ruling with one case that is different: תרומה. There the giving does count, but one should not do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So רבא splits the cases: three do not work, but תרומה does. Even so, it is forbidden, because the כהן's agreement to give it back looks like he is getting the תרומה in exchange for a favor. This split sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
He has done his duty of giving
A כהן who helps out
The threshing floors, where produce is processed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא says the תרומה gift is fine to do. It works after the fact, but doing it is forbidden.

phrases.english: with teruma, he has fulfilled the obligation of giving.
But it is forbidden to do so,
because it looks
like a priest who helps out at the threshing floors.
phrases.notes: This is a כהן who helps the farmer so he'll get the תרומה, which makes the תרומה look like payment for his help.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's statement with the one case where giving on condition of return does work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For תרומה, giving on condition of return counts as giving, but it is forbidden to do so because it looks like a כהן being paid for help at the threshing floor.

steps.title: How can רבא treat תרומה differently from the other cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: either a gift on condition of return counts as a gift, and then all the cases should work, or it does not, and then even תרומה should not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does רבא hold? If he holds that a gift on condition to return it is called a gift, then all of them should work too. And if he holds it is not called a gift, then even תרומה should not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבא's split ruling. It shows that both possible views lead to treating all the cases the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key question is whether a gift that must be given back is a real gift. Whatever the answer, it should apply to every case equally. So רבא's difference between תרומה and the others needs an explanation, which the גמרא will give next.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, he is of the opinion
A gift given on condition it be returned
It is called (counts as) a gift
All of them

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of מתנה על מנת להחזיר, a gift that must be returned, comes up in many places in הלכה, so knowing whether it counts as a gift matters far beyond this sugya.

phrases.english: What does Rava hold?

phrases.aramaic: אִי קָסָבַר מַתָּנָה עַל מְנָת לְהַחֲזִיר
phrases.english: If he holds that a gift on condition to return it
is called a gift,
then even all of them too should work.
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the sale, the woman, and the redeeming of the son from step 12.

phrases.english: And if he holds it is not called a gift,
then even teruma also should not work.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבַר רָבָא? אִי קָסָבַר מַתָּנָה עַל מְנָת לְהַחֲזִיר שְׁמָהּ מַתָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the split ruling of steps 12 and 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that תרומה works with a gift on condition of return while sale, קידושין, and פדיון הבן do not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: whether or not a gift on condition of return counts as a gift, the answer should be the same for every case, so the split seems inconsistent.

steps.title: רבא's own אתרוג ruling contradicts him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second challenge. רבא himself ruled that an אתרוג given on condition of return counts as a gift, so how can he say that such a gift does not work for buying, קידושין, or פדיון הבן?
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, רבא himself said that a gift on condition of return is a real gift. He ruled that if someone says, 'Take this אתרוג on condition that you give it back to me,' and the person takes it and gives it back, he has done the מצוה. If he does not give it back, he has not done the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is adding a second, stronger attack on רבא. It shows that רבא contradicts himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the אתרוג case, the person must own the אתרוג, and רבא says a gift on condition of return makes him the owner. So רבא clearly holds that such a gift is a real gift. That conflicts with his ruling in Step 12 that it does not work for buying, קידושין, or פדיון הבן.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: it adds a second challenge
It is called a gift, meaning it counts as a real gift
Here, take it

A gift on condition that it be returned
is called a gift!

"Here, take this etrog

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the one in Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a gift on condition of return does not work for buying, קידושין, or פדיון הבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: רבא's אתרוג ruling treats a gift on condition of return as a full gift.

steps.title: רב אשי: it works for everything except a woman
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a new version of the rule. A gift on condition of return works in every case except קידושין, because a woman cannot be acquired through חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: In all of these cases the gift works, except for a woman, because a woman cannot be acquired through חליפין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי sets aside the earlier version of the rule and gives a new one that answers both challenges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now a gift on condition of return does count as a gift, so buying, פדיון הבן, תרומה, and the אתרוג all work. קידושין is the only exception. Money that comes right back looks like חליפין, and a woman cannot be acquired that way.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: it drops the earlier approach
In all of them
It acquires, meaning it works
Symbolic exchange: a way of acquiring by handing over an item

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the gift fails in the woman's case because it is not a gift. It is a gift. The problem is that קידושין cannot be done in a way that looks like חליפין.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
In all of them, it acquires
except for a woman,
because a woman is not
acquired through exchange.
phrases.notes: In חליפין a small item is handed over just to seal the deal. Money that comes right back looks like that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both challenges by giving a new version of the rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reformulation of the ruling with one exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A gift on condition of return fails for buying, קידושין, and פדיון הבן
steps.terutzMaskana: It works everywhere except קידושין, because a woman cannot be acquired through חליפין

steps.title: רבא was quoted the way רב אשי says
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא מר בריה דרב נחמיה tells רב אשי that this is how they quote רבא in their tradition, matching רב אשי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא מר, son of רב נחמיה, said to רב אשי: That is how we say it in the name of רבא, the same as you.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone confirms that רב אשי's version of the rule is really what רבא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier version of רבא's ruling in Step 12, that the gift fails for a sale and for פדיון הבן, is set aside. Only the woman's case still fails. The accepted tradition of רבא matches רב אשי, so the contradiction with the אתרוג ruling is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: We say
In the name of
Like you, in agreement with you

steps.whatToRemember: Final rule: a gift on condition of return is a real gift and works for buying, פדיון הבן, תרומה, and אתרוג. It does not work for קידושין, because a woman cannot be acquired through חליפין.

steps.title: New ruling: 'Give a מנה to so-and-so'
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a new ruling about a woman who tells a man to give a מנה to another person. The case continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If a woman says, 'Give a מנה to so-and-so'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic. This line only sets up the case, and the ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new question is about קידושין where the money goes to someone else at the woman's request. We have to wait for the next lines to hear what רבא rules.
